lessons.title: ز (ze) — the letter that ends روز
lessons.gloss: ze — the letter that ends روز

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the sections called Script you'll notice: ز and Guided Practice until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Before the new one: write ظ and ئ once each, and name them.
Now say روز (roz), "every day". You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
ز — ze, the sound z.
It ends روز (roz), "every day". You already write ر, the short curve that drops below the line. ز (ze) is the same curve with one dot above it. Like ر, it never joins the letter after it.
1. start here: draw the independent ze downward.
2. continue curving to the left without lifting.
3. after one lift, place the dot above — and only now lift.
Pen lifts: 1.

Stroke order is one attested teaching order; hands and teachers vary. Source: Zer o Zabar, Khe, ze, zāl, swād, and zwād, independent ز calligraphic and handwriting animations and Ze instructions (Northwestern University Libraries Open Textbook, 2026).

segments.instruction: at روز and point at ز (ze) inside it
segments.source: [YOU LOOK: at **روز** and point at ز inside it]

segments.instruction: ز (ze) three times, saying z as you finish each one
segments.source: [YOU TRACE: ز three times, saying *z* as you finish each one]
[YOU WRITE: ئ, then ز, from memory]

segments.text: Which letter is this — ز? (ze, z.) Which word did it come from? (روز, roz, "every day".)

lessons.title: ط (toe) — the letter that opens طرف
lessons.gloss: toe — the letter that opens طرف

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the sections called Script you'll notice: ط and Guided Practice until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Before the new one: write ئ and ز (ze) once each, and name them.
Now say طرف (taraf), "a side, a direction". You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
ط — toe, a plain t sound, the same as ت.
It opens طرف (taraf), "a side, a direction". You already write ظ: a flat loop on the line with a tall upright stroke. ط (toe) is that shape with no dot. Urdu keeps it for words that came from Arabic.
1. start here: draw the independent to'e-series loop.
2. continue through its leftward finish without lifting.
3. after one lift, draw the tall upright — and only now lift.
Pen lifts: 1.

Stroke order is one attested teaching order; hands and teachers vary. Source: Zer o Zabar, To’e, zo’e, se, zhe, and ġhain, independent ط (toe) handwriting animation and To’e instructions (Northwestern University Libraries Open Textbook, 2026).

segments.instruction: at طرف and point at ط (toe) inside it
segments.source: [YOU LOOK: at **طرف** and point at ط inside it]

segments.instruction: ط (toe) three times, saying t as you finish each one
segments.source: [YOU TRACE: ط three times, saying *t* as you finish each one]
[YOU WRITE: ز, then ط, from memory]

segments.text: Which letter is this — ط? (toe, t.) Which word did it come from? (طرف, taraf, "a side, a direction".)
